notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics vendor evaluating Redwood Hosted API as a low-friction entry then Dedicated for predictable unit economics. Very focused on per-token costs and tail-latency for customer-facing product assistant. Open to Optimize services for batching/caching recommendations.

Conversation highlights / rep notes:
- 2025-09-17 discovery call w/ Jordan (AE), Maya (SE) + Hedgerow eng/product (CTO: Priya Rao, Head of ML: Alan Summers). Confirmed primary workloads: interactive product assistant (chat), contextual doc-search, and reranking for in-app recommendations.
- Hedgerow metrics: ~1200 daily active product users currently, targeting 5–10k DAU in 12 months; expected peak QPS ~40–60 for assistant flows.
- Latency targets: p50 <120ms, p95 <300ms for assistant; embeddings <200ms per request. Cost sensitivity: high — aiming to cap model inference spend to <$15k/mo during POC, <$50k/mo post-launch unless committed Dedicated discounts.
- Model preferences: prefer Redwood-curated open models or 3rd-party Llama-family variants; want transparent perf/quality tradeoffs. Mentioned they saw Redwood benchmark for 13B that fit their latency envelope.
- Security: SAML SSO required, SOC2 proof expected, audit logs + KMS for keys. Data residency discussion: want EU region for EU customers (Hedgerow has EMEA clients).

POC / Demo history:
- 2025-09-29 — Hosted API demo: conversation streaming, function-calling example for product metadata, quick embedding pipeline on 10k docs. Hedge: "liked streaming, token-level cost breakdown useful" (quote from Priya).
- 2025-10-01 — Small POC run with hosted traffic simulator (1k simulated users/day) to validate latencies and per-token spend. Observed higher per-token cost vs estimates due to repeated context and non-optimal batching. Logged in INF-1123.
- 2025-10-03 — Deep-dive with SE: reviewed batching/caching options, set up first Optimize workshop to estimate savings from prefix caching and continuous batching. Agreed to run quantized model variants in Dedicated POC if accuracy delta <= 1.5% on evaluation prompts.

Cost optimization specifics discussed during eval (key):
- Batching: hedgerow flows have many short-turn dialogues; SE recommended micro-batching at ingress + adaptive batching in runtime to keep p95 <300ms. Expected 18–30% token-cost reduction for assistant flows when batching is tuned.
- Caching: prefix and KV cache plans discussed. For product assistant many queries repeat; caching 30% of common prefixes estimated to reduce token spend by additional 10–20%. Need to instrument TTLs and eviction policy.
- Quantization profiles: interested in int8 and mixed-quant variants. Hedgerow will run golden prompt suite (200 prompts) to validate quality; acceptance criterion = <1.5% comprehension/regression vs FP16. SE set up INF-1198 to capture regression checks.
- Unit economics: SE ran scenario comparison (hosted vs Dedicated with committed throughput): Dedicated with 3-month commit projects 35–55% lower $/1M tokens depending on batching/caching. Hedgerow requested a worked example with their expected traffic curve.

Security/compliance notes:
- Legal requested data processing addendum and KMS integration diagram. Need SOC2 Type II evidence before production. SAML metadata exchange pending.

Customer quotes / color:
- Priya (CTO): "We need predictable costs — can't have inference bills spike during growth. If Dedicated delivers the math, we'll commit."
- Alan (Head ML): "Quantized runtimes are attractive, but we need strict accuracy checks. Show me sample outputs vs FP16 on our prompts."

Next steps (explicit):
- 10/06: Redwood to deliver worked example of monthly token spend vs Dedicated commit tiers using Hedgerow traffic forecast (Jordan).
- 10/08: Cost-optimization workshop with Engineers + Product (Maya lead) — agenda: batching knobs, cache TTLs, quantization ops, unit-econ sensitivity. Calendar invite pending.
- 10/15: Run Dedicated POC for 7 days with quantized 13B variant, measure accuracy on golden-suite and capture cost metrics.
- Legal: provide DPA and SOC2 artifacts (Redwood security to share link).

Open risks / blockers (repeat):
- Legal/data-residency proof (EU attestation).
- Need accuracy results for quantized model (<1.5% threshold).
- Final pricing/commit negotiation for Dedicated to hit target ARR math.

Misc quick items:
- References: shared pricing deck (drive link), benchmarking spreadsheet (internal).
- Demo video clip stored in fireflies ff_2025-09-29_poc-kickoff-9332.
- POC ticket INF-1198 assigned to Maya for quantization bench.
